text:
natalie: Heads-up — getting lots of noisy SLO alerts from inference-frontend traces this morning. Cost spike on OTLP egress to eu-west collectors and lots of duplicate spans. Anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

infra-bot: alert fired: otel_export_egress_cost_high (threshold 750 USD/day) — 1975000000 — affected namespaces: inference-frontend, runtime-proxy

samir: seen it. grafana panel shows OTLP throughput > 3x baseline around 04:12 UTC, aligns with a GPU node scale-up batch. wondering if SDKs are re-sending or tail-sampling botched.

kevin: noticed a pattern where traceparent header is dropped on kube-proxy -> envoy handoff for a subset of pods. when traceparent dropped we get broken spans and the gateway retries, doubling export volume.

maria: if traceparent is lost we also lose parent baggage so tail-sampler ends up keeping more traces (no parent to decide). that could explain duplicates + cost. we should redact big baggage attrs before export too (user_cookie, session_blob).

samir: for immediate mitigation can we lower SDK sampler in frontend to 0.005 and turn on attribute filtering? low risk short-term.

natalie: agree — quick patch plan: (1) SDK sample_ratio -> 0.005 (2) OTEL_ATTR_PROCESSOR drop attributes list (3) collector compression + batch_timeout tweak. I'll patch and roll canary.

maria: sample change command to patch deployment:

```
kubectl set env deployment/inference-frontend OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=probabilistic OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG=0.005 -n prod
```

kevin: also adding kube-proxy -> envoy header passthrough fix. there's a known iptables conntrack race when nodes drain fast; will add a preStop sleep 5s and passthrough rule to preserve trace headers.

dena: long-term we should avoid cross-region OTLP egress. moving collectors into each region reduces egress cost and makes sampling local. but that increases ops footprint. alternative: use per-region gateway + tail-sampling decisions in-region then forward aggregated to central store.

samir: agreed. for now can we change collector config to drop baggage and only forward score/error spans? example tweak:

```
processors:
  attributes/drop:
    actions:
      - key: user_cookie
        action: delete
      - key: session_blob
        action: delete
  probabilistic_sampler:
    sampling_percentage: 0.5
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: keep_errors
        type: error
        decision_wait: 1s
```

maria: also reduce otlp exporter flush/timeout and enable gzip:

```
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: collector.eu-west.internal:4317
    compression: gzip
    sending_queue:
      enabled: true
      num_consumers: 2
      queue_size: 5000
```

kevin: reminder — ensure `traceparent` header is in `proxy_set_header` list in the envoy config and not dropped by NLB. I pushed a small change to the lb config in staging.

natalie: i'll roll the canary in prod for frontend now, will monitor otlp egress and SLO noise. plan: 10% canary 15 min -> 50% 30 min -> full if stable. leaving alerts muted during rollout to avoid pager storms. :fire_extinguisher:

infra-bot: action created: INFRA-9509 — "temporary otel sampling + attribute filter rollout" assigned to natalie, due 1975007200

dena: follow-ups to file: (1) cost-model for cross-region trace egress (2) proposal for per-region collectors + aggregator (3) runbook for trace header loss during node drain. I'll create tasks.

samir: one more low-level note: runtime spans from the GPU inference runtime include huge KV-cache dumps under attribute `kv.state_dump` — we should avoid exporting that ever. i'll open a PR in runtime to move that to logs only.

maria: excellent — that will cut a lot. thanks all, keep us posted on canary numbers.

natalie: canary 10% up — otlp egress down ~68% so far, error trace retention down. continuing roll.

kevin: filed a tiny kube-proxy patch: add `preStop: exec: sleep 6` to avoid conntrack mid-handshake. staging looks good.

natalie: update 30m: egress now at ~20% of spike and SLO alert noise has dropped. setting follow-up meeting to design region-collector plan. thanks team! :tada:
